title: Meiosis I: Why Siblings Differ Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya's two cousins have the same mother and the same father, yet one has curly hair and the other has straight hair. If they come from the same parents, why are they not alike? Part of the answer is a division that halves the chromosomes and shuffles them.

You will see why gametes must carry one set, a zoom ladder from a flower to a homologous pair, and the five parts of prophase I running live: leptotene, zygotene (synapsis, synaptonemal complex, bivalent), pachytene (recombination nodules, crossing over), diplotene (chiasmata) and diakinesis (terminalisation). Then metaphase I, anaphase I, telophase I and interkinesis, anaphase of mitosis vs anaphase I side by side, a pause and think, six events sorted, the crossing-over exam trap, an original NEET-pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions. This is Episode 78 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
